source.title: On Dropout, Overfitting, and Interaction Effects in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Benjamin J. Lengerich; E. Xing; R. Caruana

record.file_problem: Text appears complete; some equations and figure content are garbled by extraction.
record.tranche_reason: It varies dropout rates and reports test accuracy or test error, testing when dropout affects held-out performance with a different focus and experimental setup than V6.
record.gate_note: The study also reports many interaction-effect and gradient measurements. They do not directly measure the training-to-test gap or the held-out behavior named by the claim versions, so they are not rows. Table 1 reports test accuracies; BikeShare test errors are shown only in Figure C.3 and described qualitatively.
record.test_reason: The study tests V6 in a new classification setting by comparing held-out accuracy across dropout rates on modified 20-NewsGroups. BikeShare measures regression performance and falls outside V6's classifier scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's central paraphrase is accurate: dropout preferentially suppresses higher-order interactions and can improve generalization by suppressing spurious ones. Correct the setting-specific interpretation: the stated optimal rates on modified 20-NewsGroups are 0.375, 0.25 and 0.125 for k=1, 2 and 3 respectively; zero is optimal on BikeShare.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines dropout's interaction effects using simulations and modified datasets, and reports test accuracy/error rather than the benchmark settings in V6.
record.method_sensitivity: The test outcome depends on the interaction order in modified 20-NewsGroups and on the dataset: the preferred rate decreases as k increases, and is zero for BikeShare.

fits_no_version.finding: On BikeShare regression, zero dropout gives the best test MSE; high dropout rates generalize worse than low rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout's effect on neural-network regression performance depends on the importance of true interactions and the dropout rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Analyses and interaction decompositions show that dropout preferentially suppresses higher-order interactions; these measurements do not themselves measure held-out classifier error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout regularizes higher-order interactions more strongly than lower-order interactions.

record.problems: The modified 20-NewsGroups results use five experiments; BikeShare test errors are only plotted, with no exact values in the text. The text does not specify model sizes or several training details.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Exact BikeShare values could not be recovered from the figure; only the textual comparison is recorded.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments.
Held-out error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier performance and local-connectivity explanations.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.

Convolutional classifiers, image benchmarks, very small training sets, joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation, and direct evidence that excessive dropout causes underfitting. The supplied text does not specify the modified 20-NewsGroups architecture or establish whether dropout there is exclusively input dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removals.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 reports means and standard deviations over five experiments, not significance tests. Compare rates within each k; accuracies across k represent tasks of different difficulty. The study is not an original source for V6.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Generalization as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Fully connected and convolutional image-classification regimes, very small training sets, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the training-to-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
